scope: Six existing upstream builder/component routes; partial #2510/#2926 delivery, no new managed ownership or stage promotion

steps.title: Prepare a player with upstream setup
steps.instruction: The official Installation.zip is a source and setup kit, not a ready-made player. On Windows, install the upstream LLVM 22.1-or-newer, Visual Studio 2026 C++/Windows SDK, CMake 4.2-or-newer, Git and Ninja prerequisites, extract the kit into a separate retained source folder, then deliberately run Build.cmd and select your own US Xbox XISO (.iso or .xiso). A full-disc dump needs upstream conversion first. The builder acquires dependencies and builds the player. Portcove does not run it during discovery.

steps.title: Register the completed player
steps.instruction: When the upstream build succeeds, use Open game folder and choose b2.exe with that folder as its working directory in Portcove. Save the launch details, then choose Play separately. For Linux use upstream Install.desktop; macOS uses Install.command and its Xcode/macOS prerequisites. These experimental native platforms have separate dependency/build instructions; Windows package inspection does not qualify them. Keep source, build and data folders together, and rerun upstream setup after moving them.

steps.title: Back up and rebuild when updating
steps.instruction: You or upstream own the runtime, generated game files and updates. Before updating, close the game and builder and back up data/user, data/local/settings.cfg and any data/local/custom-music beside the player. Extract updated source over the retained source folder while keeping build and data, then deliberately rerun the platform setup with your own XISO. Keep the old working copy and originals recoverable. Portcove external registration leaves files untouched and supplies no managed Update, Backup or Rollback.

entries.fit_disposition: Official Installation.zip is source/setup, with external compiler/dependency/XISO preparation and retained source/build coordinates. Current native-portable replacement does not perform this build. Useful upstream setup remains selected; reconsider management on an official independently replaceable player or supported existing preparation contract.

steps.title: Prepare the game with the upstream Builder
steps.instruction: The portable download is ActRaiser Recomp Builder, not a prepared player. For a Windows or macOS portable desktop bundle, extract it into a writable folder, keep its .portable marker and BuilderData together, then deliberately open ActRaiserRecompBuilder.exe on Windows or the matching Builder app’s Workshop. The generic Linux x64 tar.xz uses ./run-build.sh to open the Workshop in your browser; follow its upstream prerequisites. Choose your own supported USA ActRaiser ROM and Build game. The bundle supplies its compiler; Portcove does not run it during discovery. Use the matching package and instructions for your platform.

steps.title: Add the completed game
steps.instruction: The default output is ActRaiserRecomp beside the Builder. Choose the completed game executable in that output folder in Portcove, with its folder as the working directory. Keep its DLLs, user-rom.sfc, tools, assets, settings and saves together. Save launch details, then choose Play separately. If application control blocks a builder tool, retain its error and use upstream/administrator guidance.

steps.title: Back up and rebuild to update
steps.instruction: You or upstream own the generated player and updates. Close the game and back up its entire saves directory before using the new Builder’s Update existing installation to rebuild that game folder. Upstream migrates older save.srm/save.ini or actraiser.srm to Slot 1 and keeps originals under saves/legacy-layout. Use Import previous installation for older utils layouts. Moving between portable and per-user storage does not transfer data automatically. Keep the working copy recoverable. External registration leaves every file untouched; Portcove supplies no managed Update, Backup or Rollback.

entries.fit_disposition: Official portable archive is a ROM compiler/Workshop, not a prepared player. Game replacement rebuilds generated code and has explicit legacy saves/storage migration. steps.title: Prepare either game with the shared launcher
steps.instruction: Extract the whole official package. Choose GoldenSunLauncher.exe on Windows, or GoldenSunLauncher on Linux, then choose The Broken Seal or The Lost Age and your own matching USA/Europe GBA ROM. Keep the normal SHA-1 ROM check enabled. No GBA BIOS is required. The bundled compiler prepares game code on first launch and after updates; Linux also needs system SDL2 and OpenGL. Portcove does not run this builder during discovery.

steps.title: Register the collection launcher
steps.instruction: Choose the shared launcher and its folder as the working directory in Portcove. Save launch details, then choose Play separately. Keep the complete collection together, including the per-game builders and generated output. This remains one collection identity for both games. Upstream reports public-testing bugs; successful preparation is not completed gameplay qualification.

steps.title: Keep current data and rebuild after updates
steps.instruction: You or upstream own this external player. The launcher offers a newer release download; it does not make this a managed Portcove Update. Close both games and retain your working folder before updating. Back up ROMs, Saves (including Saves/Imported), Controls, Music mods, and the per-game settings under games, plus any custom paths. The launcher keeps original imported saves and puts conflicts under Saves/Imported. A new version can rebuild game code from your ROM. Runtime replacement does not rewind saves or guarantee savestate compatibility. Keep original-containing data private. External registration preserves every file and supplies no managed Backup or Rollback.

entries.fit_disposition: The collection rebuilds game libraries from two ROM workflows after updates; generated output, shared data and games-specific settings must agree. The Netflix Games version is not supported. Keep this prepared folder separate from your only working copy.

steps.title: Register the prepared player
steps.instruction: Choose the actual matching engine executable after upstream setup, with its prepared game folder as the working directory. Game.dll is a module, not a launch target. Read-only discovery and downloading do not run or combine modules/helpers. Upstream’s save-transfer guidance can bring over your own original PC save data; keep a separate original copy. Keep your actual save data, settings and mods with that prepared folder. Save launch details first, then choose Play separately.

This download is a game module rather than a complete player, so finish pairing it through upstream before registering.

selected_release.name: RSDKv5 + U 1.1.1
selected_release.body:
New minor release with a few improvements and bugfixes:
* `Settings.ini` now always gets created on Switch/Android platforms for easier modification
* Fix inaccurate scene switching in rare scenarios
* ModAPI: Fixed memory corruption when using `GetSettingsString`/`SetSettingsString`
* Linux: Fixed empty logs/ini files on some distros
* DX11: Fix crash when no shaders were found (mainly in legacy mode)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/RSDKModding/RSDKv5-Decompilation/compare/v1.1.0...v1.1.1

**As a reminder, release builds and autobuilds lock the ability to use Origins Plus DLC content. If you'd like to enable it, you will need to [manually build the decompilation](https://github.com/RSDKModding/RSDKv5-Decompilation#how-to-build).**

steps.title: Let the upstream launcher prepare your own game
steps.instruction: The recommended Windows download is the upstream lawn/Z3R Launcher setup package. Open that installer deliberately after downloading, then use its guided preparation. Install its published package for your platform, choose your own clean USA A Link to the Past .sfc, and follow its setup/extract/build steps. The Windows setup package includes the lightweight Git/Python/TCC/SDL2 toolkit; choosing a separate MSBuild route needs its own build tools. Linux and macOS use their matching upstream dependency guide. Portcove does not install these tools or run the launcher during discovery. When setup finishes, register the prepared zelda3.exe on Windows or native zelda3 player on Linux/macOS with its project folder as the working directory, then choose Play explicitly.

steps.title: Keep the generated assets and player data together
steps.instruction: Keep the complete prepared project, your original ROM, zelda3_assets.dat, zelda3.user.ini overrides, saves, custom sprites/shaders/MSU packs, and any randomizer YAML, seed/spoiler files or selected feature-asset folders separately backed up. The game tries zelda3.user.ini before zelda3.ini. Keep packaged defaults with their own release and use user overrides for personal settings. The native release ZIP supplies a player and SDL but no generated zelda3_assets.dat; copying that executable alone is not finished setup.

steps.title: Regenerate matching assets when updating
steps.instruction: Let the selected upstream launcher manage its own project setup and updates. The game’s guide requires asset regeneration after relevant executable/source, extraction-script, YAML or INI behavior changes. Copying an older generated asset file into a replacement runtime cannot satisfy that requirement. Preserve the old prepared copy and randomizer choices before regeneration; extracting clean ROM data after randomizing overwrites the randomized YAML. Portcove registers the prepared player without claiming Update, Backup or Rollback for these externally owned files. The related Python Z3R-Launcher and current lawn delivery are helpers for this same engine identity, not extra games. The launcher’s Updates action uses its matching platform installer or self-replacement route; keep that owner. Its download feed follows releases without a fixed tag in this listing.

entries.fit_disposition: The related lawn launcher owns installer/self-update and original-ROM project extraction/build. Game assets must be regenerated on relevant source/YAML/INI changes; preserving arbitrary old zelda3_assets.dat would not satisfy that protocol. Retain richer upstream setup; no competing native-portable owner. Helpers remain the same game identity.
